headline: Chips Surge, Software Stumbles as Jobs Data Reshapes Friday's Tape
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a split note, with semiconductors decisively capturing the day's narrative after a hotter-than-expected jobs report sent the two-year Treasury yield to its highest mark since January 2025. Traders interpreted the strong labor data as ammunition for a potential Federal Reserve rate move, reshaping positioning across the board and driving a sharp wedge between cyclical chip names and rate-sensitive software stocks. Of the 545 names in our universe, 300 finished higher against 242 decliners — a modestly positive breadth reading that masked the violence beneath the surface.

The sector rotation was stark. Semiconductors led every cohort with a gain of 3.05%, followed at a distance by Industrials at 0.87% and Materials at 0.82%. Software bore the brunt of the selling, shedding 1.25%, while Healthcare dropped 0.74% and Energy gave back 0.34%. Homebuilders slipped 0.27%, unsurprising given the rate-rise backdrop that pressured mortgage-sensitive names.

Sandisk was the session's undisputed standout, surging 11.9% to top the leaderboard, with Semtech and KLA Corp adding 9.22% and 7.32% respectively. At the other extreme, Fair Isaac cratered 16.68% and UiPath fell 16.63%, a twin collapse in financial-data and automation software that underscored just how selective Friday's rally truly was.

briefs.headline: Jobs Beat Lifts Two-Year Yield to 16-Month High
briefs.body: A stronger-than-anticipated labor market report pushed the two-year Treasury yield to its loftiest level since January 2025, reigniting debate over whether the Federal Reserve might resume rate increases. The data rattled rate-sensitive corners of the equity market, particularly software and long-duration growth names, while cyclical sectors absorbed the news with relative composure.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac and UiPath Post Session's Sharpest Declines
briefs.body: Fair Isaac and UiPath each shed more than 16% on Friday, making them the two worst performers in our universe by a wide margin. The parallel collapse across financial-data analytics and enterprise automation software suggested investors are reassessing stretched valuations in niches where AI displacement risk and rising discount rates compound pressure simultaneously.

briefs.headline: Sandisk Rockets Nearly 12% to Crown the Semiconductor Rally
briefs.body: Memory-chip maker Sandisk was Friday's top gainer, climbing 11.9% and anchoring a broad-based move higher across the semiconductor complex. FormFactor rose 7.38% and KLA Corp gained 7.32%, signaling that investors rotated aggressively into chip-equipment and component names as a perceived haven within the technology universe.

briefs.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Simmer as Iran Pressure Mounts
briefs.body: The White House signaled a potential military strike near Iran, while the United States and allied governments pressed the IAEA board to refer Iran to the UN Security Council. Separately, Washington sanctioned a Turkish bank and two subsidiaries as part of its broader Iran pressure campaign, adding another layer of geopolitical uncertainty heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: U.S. Clears $5 Billion Munitions Sale to Saudi Arabia
briefs.body: American authorities approved a potential sale of extended-range precision munitions to Saudi Arabia valued at roughly five billion in the latest defense transaction tied to Middle East security arrangements. The approval arrives amid elevated regional tensions involving Iran and continued diplomatic activity around the Ukraine conflict, with senior U.S. envoys dispatched abroad for peace discussions.

briefs.headline: Bloom Energy Stands Out Among Non-Chip Friday Winners
briefs.body: Fuel-cell developer Bloom Energy advanced 7.35% on Friday, carving out a notable gain in a session otherwise dominated by semiconductor names. The move gave Bloom a rare spot on the top-gainers list alongside chip peers, suggesting selective investor appetite for clean-energy infrastructure plays even as broader energy-sector returns remained slightly negative on the day.
